skill.name: set-up-shopify-chatgpt-ads-customer-matching
skill.description: Guide Shopify merchants through customer data matching for ChatGPT Ads using Product Metrics. The guide covers connection checks, consent settings, and test order delivery through the OpenAI Conversions API.
skill.summary: Configure and check Shopify customer matching for ChatGPT Ads through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: The reconnaissance alerts and most backtick alerts describe ordinary setup documentation or read-only checks. Real risks include broad order reads, an unpinned installer, and reliance on a remote API and mutable fallback documentation. The workflow lacks safeguards for credential entry, browser handoffs, and approval before customer data sharing begins.

remediation.issue: The credential instructions allow assistant handling of API keys.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter keys in the verified Product Metrics app. Remove exceptions that allow chat or command arguments to carry raw credentials.

remediation.issue: The setup enables delivery before the consent source is checked.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the vendor, destination, and hashed and unhashed fields before setup. Verify the store, pixel, and consent source, then require explicit merchant approval before enabling delivery. Test both consent and refusal with controlled orders.

remediation.issue: Browser handoffs trust a URL returned by a tool.
remediation.suggestion: Validate HTTPS and the expected service origin before sharing a handoff link. If the link cannot be verified, direct the user to the known dashboard instead.

remediation.issue: Order checks can retrieve more data than delivery verification needs.
remediation.suggestion: Use a known test order and return only its delivery status. Avoid broad order listings and omit unrelated order fields from assistant context.

remediation.issue: The installer can run or fetch unpinned software.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the installer version and skill revision. Keep installation an explicit user action and use reviewed builds.

remediation.issue: Remote tools and documentation can change after the skill is reviewed.
remediation.suggestion: Use bundled references or a reviewed revision. Require explicit approval for remote MCP access and restrict it to the documented methods needed for this workflow.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Can Enter Assistant and Command Context
semantic_findings.description: The main skill permits requesting an OpenAI Conversions API key and passing it directly to a command. The connection guide instead tells users never to paste the key into chat. No protected input method is required, so the key could appear in assistant transcripts, command logs, or process arguments.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The credential exception conflicts with the no-chat instruction. The reviewed files do not define a secure path for the command to receive the key.

semantic_findings.title: Customer Data Sharing Can Begin Before Consent Setup Review
semantic_findings.description: The workflow uses Product Metrics even if the merchant has not requested that vendor. It instructs merchants to leave event delivery on before verifying the consent source. Matching is automatic after connection and can include unhashed network and browser identifiers alongside hashed customer fields.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The references put connection before consent configuration and list fields that are sent without hashing. They describe per-event consent checks, so this is a setup risk, not evidence of an actual consent bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Unverified Browser Handoff Links
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the merchant to open a browser URL from a setup response without requiring an origin check. A compromised or incorrect response could direct the merchant to a lookalike login or authorization page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The handoff directly uses the returned URL and specifies no trusted destination check. No evidence of a malicious URL was found.

content.user_title: Set Up Shopify Customer Matching for ChatGPT Ads
content.value_statement: Shopify orders can be difficult to attribute when browser tracking misses a conversion. This guide helps you review consent settings and check delivery to ChatGPT Ads through Product Metrics.
actual_capabilities: Check Shopify and ChatGPT Ads setup status using the Product Metrics CLI or MCP server.
Identify missing prerequisites and show which steps the merchant completes in Shopify or Ads Manager.
Locate the consent configuration and explain how marketing and ad storage consent affect delivery.
Guide the merchant through checking a paid test order and finding delivery errors.
Describe which customer fields are hashed and which fields Product Metrics can send without hashing.
limitations: Requires a connected Shopify store, an active Product Metrics subscription, and a ChatGPT Ads destination for live verification.
Base tracking setup and bidding changes are outside this skill's scope.
Delivery status does not show the hashed fields or prove an individual match.
The integration does not import historical orders or revise events after later refunds and cancellations.

use_cases.title: Review Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Check whether your Shopify store, subscription, and ChatGPT Ads connection are ready before enabling event delivery.

use_cases.title: Investigate Missing Conversions
use_cases.description: Check whether a paid test order appears in Product Metrics and identify consent or delivery errors.

use_cases.title: Review Data Sharing
use_cases.description: Compare the documented matching fields and consent requirements with your store's privacy settings before sharing data.

prompt_templates.title: List the Prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: What do I need before I can use customer matching for ChatGPT Ads on Shopify? Explain which accounts and permissions I need.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are planning the setup and have not connected any accounts.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup Without Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Check the connection status for my selected Shopify store and ChatGPT Ads pixel in Product Metrics. Report missing prerequisites without changing settings.
prompt_templates.scenario: You want to know what is already connected.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Paid Test Order
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through checking delivery for one paid test order. Use only that order and report the delivery status without sharing customer details.
prompt_templates.scenario: You have placed a test order and want to confirm delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Review Consent and Matching Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: List the hashed and unhashed fields Product Metrics can send to ChatGPT Ads. Explain what should happen when a shopper declines marketing or ad storage consent.
prompt_templates.scenario: You are reviewing data sharing before enabling the destination.

output_examples.input: Product Metrics shows my pixel as connected. What should I check next?
output: In Tracking, open Configure consent and confirm it matches the banner your Shopify store shows.
After approving delivery, use a paid test order with marketing consent. Check whether it appears under OpenAI Conversions API.
A delivered event does not prove that ChatGPT Ads matched the order to a shopper.

output_examples.input: Why did the test order that declined marketing cookies not appear?
output: The documented behavior is to withhold the event when the shopper declines marketing consent.
If an order with marketing consent is missing too, check the configured consent source and look for a delivery error in Product Metrics.

best_practices: Confirm the store, Ads pixel, and consent source before approving event delivery.
Enter the Conversions API key only in the verified Product Metrics app.
Use controlled paid test orders to verify behavior with and without marketing consent.
anti_patterns: Pasting a Conversions API key into chat or adding it to a prompt.
Treating hashed customer data as anonymous or assuming all transmitted fields are hashed.
Using recent customer orders to test delivery when a controlled test order is available.

faq.question: Is there a separate customer matching switch?
faq.answer: No. Product Metrics automatically includes eligible matching fields once ChatGPT Ads is connected and the required consent is present.

faq.question: Which shopper data is hashed?
faq.answer: Product Metrics documents hashing email, phone, name, and customer ID. Postal code, country, IP address, and user agent can be sent without hashing.

faq.question: What consent is needed?
faq.answer: Events need marketing consent. Click and browser references also need ad storage consent. Events are marked as opted out when ad personalization consent is absent.

faq.question: Where can I confirm delivery?
faq.answer: Open Tracking, then OpenAI Conversions API in Product Metrics. Look for your paid test order and check for delivery errors.

faq.question: Can I see the hashed fields or confirm a match?
faq.answer: No. There is no report of the hashed fields, and delivery status does not confirm an individual match.

faq.question: Will this import past orders or update refunded conversions?
faq.answer: No. Historical orders are not imported. Later refunds and cancellations do not revise events already sent to ChatGPT Ads.
